sense: of an attempt or a plan: turning out as hoped

terms.comment: With a verb: prosperē ēvenīre, prosperē prōcēdere, to turn out well (Liv. 23.27.12; Cic. Fam. 12.9.2; Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: to be successful, to work, to go well (of a thing attempted)
terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, intransitive; in this sense mostly in the third person
evidence: Ter. And. 670: hāc nōn successit, aliā aggrediēmur viā
Caes. BG 7.26: quod rēs nūlla successerat (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Latin says “it succeeded” where English says “it was successful”.

terms.gloss: to turn out well, to succeed
evidence: Cic. Fam. 12.9.2: omnia prosperē prōcēdent (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Phil. 5.40: et bene et fēlīciter gesta (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Successfully is fēlīciter; a success, rēs fēlīciter or bene gesta (Traupman 387).

phrases.latin: Dēceptus sum, at nōn dēfatīgātus. … Hāc nōn successit, aliā aggrediēmur viā.
phrases.english: I’ve been foiled, but I’m not worn out. … It didn’t work this way; we’ll go at it by another road.

phrases.latin: ut ōrsīs tantum operis successūs prosperōs darent
phrases.english: that they might grant success to so great a work now begun
